description.role: Lower-cost default for routine work and bounded investigation within an established architecture.
use_when: Routine implementation, small or medium changes, tests, and configuration with clear requirements.
Ordinary debugging and local correctness reviews with a bounded scope.
Straightforward explanations, summaries, and editing human-facing text without substantial ambiguity.
not_for: Architectural direction, difficult debugging, security-critical decisions, or interacting failure modes.
Demanding human-facing writing or recommendations requiring nuanced judgment and synthesis.
description.boundary: Prefer Sol whenever it adequately covers the task. Higher reasoning effort does not expand its scope; use Astra when substantive judgment or complex ambiguity is central.

description.role: Higher-cost reasoning and writing model for complex work requiring substantive judgment.
use_when: Architecture, design trade-offs, ambiguous requirements, and high-stakes technical recommendations.
Difficult debugging, cross-cutting changes, interacting failure modes, and security-critical decisions.
Demanding human-facing writing, nuanced technical specifications, and synthesis requiring careful judgment.
not_for: Routine implementation, tests, configuration, or bounded debugging that Sol can handle.
Simple explanations, summaries, and mechanical prose edits.
description.boundary: Choose Astra when Sol's scope is insufficient, not merely because the prompt mentions review, planning, or writing.
